# AI Film Knowledge Base

Repository: https://github.com/62656456/ai-film-knowledge-base

Canonical knowledge language: Simplified Chinese.

Public corpus: 105 Markdown notes.

Read directly on GitHub; no private vault, database import, or companion Skill is required.

Start with:
- README.md
- CATALOG.md
- knowledge/00-总纲/
- knowledge/A-理论层/
- knowledge/B-实战层/
- knowledge/C-审核与验收层/
- docs/VISUAL_ASSETS.md

Routing:
- Use A (51 notes) for cinematography, directing, screenwriting, and durable film-language theory.
- Use B (43 notes) for storyboard, prompt, shot, action, and bounded platform practice.
- Use C (7 notes) for status, evidence, input freezing, directed return, AI-film acceptance, independent Skill review, and public knowledge/image gates.
- Use one note independently when it answers the task; do not require the complete corpus.

Review rule: file existence, content review, real-output evidence, and designated-reviewer acceptance are different states. A failure should return to the earliest broken decision with the failed gate, observed evidence, protected passing items, required correction, and resubmission proof.

Evidence rule: keep stable mechanisms, source-backed interpretations, practical methods, candidate methods, time-sensitive facts, and unknowns distinct. Recheck changing platform facts against current primary sources. Do not infer unavailable linked content.

Image rule: 696 source teaching images are published under docs/assets/examples/ with 730 placements in 41 knowledge notes, alongside ten public-method SVGs. Maintainer publication authorization was explicit on 2026-10-20. Use docs/IMAGE_MANIFEST.json for file, purpose, license, hash and note locations; use docs/IMAGE_GALLERY.md for visual browsing. Illustrations are educational constructions, not original film frames or proof of actual production parameters. knowledge/ remains Markdown-only.

Public boundary: do not infer, request, or reconstruct personal projects, private retrospectives, private AI infrastructure, private validation evidence, inspiration archives, raw chats, session identifiers, local paths, or source-vault image files.
